comments.author: @thomasstuart1825
comments.text:
I can see the potential in the digital workload, but I cringed and Lmao when I saw the video of pulsing pistachios with the shells on! I hope people are going to be scrutinizing videos that they look at and not accepting them point blank... or verbatim instructions. Also, the finessing will probably get better... but I thought it was slightly weird that the AI call phrases talked over the restaurant employee at certain parts. I have seen demos where models have the interrupt feature... but unless there is wide adoption of agents for concierge/secretary service, I could see there being a growing problem with human recipients of AI calls if the human is stressed, rushed, or otherwise not in a leisurely conversational pace and mood. AI improvements will probably smooth this stuff out, but I'm wary that the current product would yield some issues.

 Another thought... this is probably obvious, but I can imagine the main AI companies are already working on their own agent stacks. This seems like a temporary use scenario. Once the other companies have their own agent products on the market as well, this will probably seem redundant or obsolete. These companies would have to make sure that they still advance other models' utility or provide more sophisticated offerings to stay relevant.
